events.object: Dowager ( or Imperial Pelican ) Fabergé egg
events.quote: made under the supervision of the Russian jeweller Peter Carl Fabergé in 1898

events.text: Nicholas II presented the egg to his mother on Easter 1898.
events.subject: self
events.quote: who presented it to his mother , the Dowager Empress Maria Feodorovna on Easter 1898

events.text: The Pelican Egg was presented to Maria Feodorovna for Easter 1898.
events.subject: self
events.quote: this Egg was presented to Maria Feodorovna for Easter 1898 .

events.text: In 1930, the Imperial Pelican Fabergé egg was one of ten Imperial eggs sold by the Antikvariat to Armand Hammer in New York City.
events.subject: self
events.quote: In 1930 , the Imperial Pelican Fabergé egg , with the eight oval miniatures , was one of ten Imperial eggs sold

events.text: The egg was purchased by Lillian Thomas Pratt from Hammer Galleries between 1936 and 1938.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Between 1936 and 1938 it was purchased by Lillian Thomas Pratt , the wife of John Lee Pratt , from Hammer Galleries .

events.text: Mrs. Pratt willed the Egg to the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts in Richmond, Virginia, upon her death in 1947.
events.subject: self
events.quote: Mrs . Pratt willed the Egg to the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts in Richmond , Virginia , upon her death in 1947 .
